_comment: The CONTRACT for Hermes learning packets. Data, not code (Kimi 2026-08-13 Q2c: a hardcoded schema is not inspectable or diffable). scripts/hermes-learning-validate.mjs reads this; any emitter must satisfy it. Bump schema_version on any change to required_* and record why in changelog.

required_frontmatter_from._comment: Keys required only for packets dated on/after this ISO date. Retro-requiring fields on historical packets would make migration impossible and turn the validator into permanent noise.

required_headings._comment: Matched LITERALLY at line start. hermes-closeout-gate.mjs matches '## Mistakes I made' exactly - a numbered '## 6. Mistakes I made' does NOT match and silently reads as 'nothing went wrong'. That defect shipped 2026-08-13.

mistake_terminal_state._comment: Fable ruling 2026-08-23, from the 2,523-bullet forensics corpus: 38-47% of recorded errors had ALREADY been written up before they recurred, and 'third time session' appears 13 times. Writing a lesson down is not a fix - the corpus proves it at scale. Every mistake bullet must therefore terminate in a DECISION about a mechanism, not in prose. Three legal terminal states, one of which must appear in each bullet. This makes 'write it down harder' - the meta-recurrence - structurally impossible to express. Date-scoped like required_frontmatter_from: history is never retro-failed, because a gate that blocks the wrong person gets switched off.
mistake_terminal_state._from_comment: Deliberately TOMORROW, not today. Set to 2026-08-23 first and it retro-failed 7 packets written earlier the same day by other agents' in-flight sessions - work that was correct under the contract that existed when it was written. That is precisely the failure this schema keeps warning about: a gate that blocks the wrong person gets switched off. Effective from the first full day after the rule exists.

marker_meanings.MECHANISM:: a command, hook, test, or gate was created or updated so this cannot recur silently - name it
marker_meanings.LORE:: no mechanism is buildable for this; explicitly accepted as judgement-only, and the reason why
marker_meanings.MERGED:: folded into an existing mechanism - name which one

mistake_terminal_state._empty_comment: An honest-empty section ('## Mistakes I made - none surfaced this task') has no bullets and so trips nothing. Never omit the heading: an absent section reads as 'nothing went wrong'.

tier_allowlist._comment: FAIL-CLOSED. Sub-Fable output must never enter the durable corpus (Rule 68). Sean's designation 2026-08-10 widened this to Opus 5 and Kimi K3.

lifecycle._comment: Kimi 2026-08-13 finding 6: status existed in 6/18 packets with no state machine - 'enterprise knowledge without review is a rumor mill with frontmatter'. Advancing past 'reviewed' requires a reviewed_by value.

privacy_forbidden_patterns._comment: Write-time guard only. Rule 44/59. The repo-history scan is a separate one-time job (Kimi finding 5) - this does NOT cover it.

warnings._comment: Warn, never gate. Kimi Q2/section 2: gating on a field present in 5/18 packets is wrong.
warnings._strict_yaml_comment: Frontmatter that our naive parser accepts but a standards-compliant YAML parser rejects. WARNING not error, for two reasons: several failing packets belong to other agents' in-flight sessions and gating would block work that is not theirs to fix; and the parser (js-yaml) is NOT a declared dependency, so the check can be unavailable. When unavailable the tool says so explicitly - absence of a strict warning never implies conformance. Set false to disable.

changelog.why: First contract. Motivated by 18 packets carrying 8 distinct frontmatter shapes, because every packet was hand-written from memory and no validator existed. Kimi K3 ranked this the single highest-value thing to build: the validator is the contract, the emitter is merely one producer of it, and a validator that only accepts emitter output cannot migrate the existing corpus.

Added the strict_yaml warning. No change to required_* - additive warning only, so no packet that passed 1.0.0 fails 1.1.0. Motivated by a measured contradiction: the corpus satisfied this contract while 8 packets were unreadable to any standards-compliant YAML parser, because parseFrontmatter is deliberately naive. A ninth was produced by our own corrective pass, which emitted a colon-space inside an unquoted scalar - the naive parser accepted it, so nothing caught it until a real parser was run by hand. Kept as a WARNING because several failing packets belong to other agents' live sessions and a gate that blocks the wrong person gets switched off.

Added mistake_terminal_state. Date-scoped from 2026-08-24 (deliberately the day AFTER it shipped - scoping it to the same day retro-failed 7 packets written earlier that day by other agents), so no packet that passed 1.1.0 fails 1.2.0. Motivated by the failure-forensics corpus (2,523 self-reported mistake bullets across 106 packets + 1,109 memos): 38-47% of recorded errors had already been written up BEFORE they recurred, 'already written' appears 41 times, and 'third time session' 13 times - agents repeating a mistake three times inside one session, with the lesson on disk. The measured catch profile is ~84 caught by running/checking, ~26 by reading at the moment of act, ~65 by adversarial rounds, and rule-recall negligible. Fable 5's Final-Decider ruling: change the TERMINAL STATE of a lesson. A bullet may no longer end in prose; it must end in MECHANISM / LORE / MERGED. The point is not bookkeeping - it is that 'I will be more careful' becomes inexpressible in the corpus, which is the single most-repeated failure the corpus records about itself.
